text:
Anya (Sales): Heads-up, RetailBank POC failing when they call our private endpoint from behind their corporate outbound proxy. They see 502s and cert errors. Can eng help triage?

Jamal (Eng): Quick question: are they using a forward proxy that terminates TLS (TLS-inspection) or a CONNECT tunnel?

Anya (Sales): Their infra lead says "inline proxy" and that egress goes through an appliance that does TLS interception for outbound domains.

Ravi (NetOps): That will break SNI and certs unless the proxy does CONNECT. Can you paste a curl and an openssl s_client capture from their test host?

Anya (Sales): Pasted both from their dev VM (they masked real IPs):
```
$ curl -v https://rb-poc.internal.redwood/v1/status
* Rebuilt URL to: https://rb-poc.internal.redwood/v1/status\n*   Trying 10.20.30.5...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to rb-poc.internal.redwood (10.20.30.5) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=corp-proxy.local
* SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'rb-poc.internal.redwood'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (corp-proxy.local) does not match target host name 'rb-poc.internal.redwood'
```

Openssl: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.5:443 -servername rb-poc.internal.redwood
CONNECTED(00000005)\ndepth=0 CN = corp-proxy.local\nverify return:1\n---\nCertificate chain\n 0 s:/CN=corp-proxy.local\n   i:/CN=corp-proxy-ca\n---\nServer certificate\nsubject=/CN=corp-proxy.local\nissuer=/CN=corp-proxy-ca\n---\nNo client certificate CA names sent\n---\nSSL handshake has read 3872 bytes and written 517 bytes\n---\n```
They also tried `curl --resolve rb-poc.internal.redwood:443:10.20.30.5` and the same proxy cert shows up.

Jamal (Eng): Ok that's classic TLS interception. The proxy is terminating TLS and presenting its own cert (corp-proxy.local). Two problems for us: 1) SNI the proxy sends to our backend might be different (or missing), so the endpoint-router serves default cert; 2) the client's effective source IP is the proxy appliance, which can confuse allowlists and rate limits.

Katy (Security): From a compliance POV they should either use a TLS passthrough (CONNECT) for this POC domain or add an exception in the proxy for rb-poc.internal.redwood. We cannot accept customer private CA certs on our side.

Ravi (NetOps): Also saw in our logs their calls were mapped to a single NAT IP (10.99.8.7) and hitting rate limiting on the POC tenant because multiple devs share the same egress IP. That explains intermittent 429s they reported earlier.

Anya (Sales): They said they can't disable interception globally; security policy forbids it for most hosts. They can add an allowlist entry for a narrow set of domains. Is that enough?

Jamal (Eng): Yes. Two recommended short-term fixes for the POC: 
- Add a proxy exception so the client's connection uses CONNECT (no MITM): proxy needs to allow CONNECT to our ENI IPs and port 443. That preserves SNI and cert chain.
- If CONNECT impossible, customer can add our endpoint to the proxy skip-list and also ensure their proxy forwards SNI and the original Host header. If the proxy rewrites SNI or Host, TLS will fail.

Ravi (NetOps): Also ask them to add our POC egress IPs to their firewall allowlist (we provided the ENI IPs in onboarding) and to whitelist our health probe and control-plane CIDR or our checks will be dropped.

Anya (Sales): They tried a `curl -x` through the proxy and `curl -v --proxy-insecure` and still got the proxy cert. They claim they added CONNECT rules but still see interception.

Jamal (Eng): If their appliance is configured to break TLS even for CONNECT (some DLP appliances do that by acting as a forward proxy after CONNECT), they'll need to either: 1) create a specific exception for rb-poc.internal.redwood that disables interception and preserves SNI, or 2) tunnel traffic over a bastion/VPN so the proxy never sees the TLS handshake.

Katy (Security): Reminder: we cannot ask customers to share private keys. They must either add the exception or accept the VPN/bastion route.

Anya (Sales): RetailBank PM prefers exception over VPN. They asked if we can accept their proxy CA as trusted by our router so certs match.

Jamal (Eng): We don't accept arbitrary third-party CAs into our trust store for hosted Private endpoints. That would be a massive security/PKI risk. Not an option.

Ravi (NetOps): Operational checklist for them to unblock POC: 
- Add `rb-poc.internal.redwood` to proxy exemption list (no TLS inspection).
- Ensure their proxy allows CONNECT and forwards SNI/Host unchanged.
- Whitelist our ENI IPs and health-probe CIDR in their egress firewall.
- If their egress NAT collapses many clients into one IP, request a larger SNAT pool or we can temporarily relax per-IP rate limits for the POC (support ticket needed).

infra-bot: support:temporary-rate-limit-exemption ticket 1800456901 created for project:retailbank-poc

Anya (Sales): I asked them to do the proxy exception and send confirmation. They responded they opened a change with their proxy team; ETA for rule is 8 hours.

Jamal (Eng): After they flip the rule, ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.5:443 -servername rb-poc.internal.redwood` again and confirm the server cert shows our CN/public SAN and not corp-proxy.local. Also include `curl -v` output.

(8 hours later) Anya (Sales): Update from RetailBank - proxy exception applied, we retested and now see the correct cert and no 502s. They still had one 429 due to shared SNAT but infra-bot ticket opened.

Ravi (NetOps): Confirmed on our side: requests now show proper SNI and the customer IPs match their expected ranges. We applied temporary rate-limit exemption while they expand SNAT.

Katy (Security): Verified no private CAs were uploaded and their proxy exception was minimum scope. Good to close.

Anya (Sales): Closing here. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
